title: 2012 HMMT February Combinatorics Problem 1
statement:
In the game of Minesweeper, a number on a square denotes the number of mines that share at least one vertex with that square. A square with a number may not have a mine, and the blank squares are undetermined. How many ways can the mines be placed in this configuration?

|  |  |  |  |  |  |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
|  | 2 |  | 1 |  | 2 |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |

solutions.text: 95 Let \(A\) be the number of mines in the first two columns. Let \(B, C, D, E\) be the number of mines in the third, fourth, fifth, and sixth columns, respectively. We need to have \(A+B=2\), \(B+C+D=1\), and \(D+E=2\). This can happen in three ways, which are \((A, B, C, D, E)=\) \((2,0,1,0,2),(2,0,0,1,1),(1,1,0,0,2)\). This gives \((10)(2)(1)+(10)(3)(2)+(5)(3)(1)=95\) possible configurations.
